title: W6: a team's own memory, and corrections that reach exactly the team work resting on the old fact
request: Build W6 of the collaborative workspace plan: a team memory scope (dclab_core memory v3 reading v2 and v1, team_scope_id, team ids on the authorized scope, a team's own editable base, a team summary for members only, a deliberate share into the problem base with its source), and the owner's 50 to 30 correction test: Sales corrects capacity, every task, report and decision citing the old fact revision becomes stale, Business is alerted in its thread through the W3 post, the decision waits for its owner's review, and untouched work and the kitchen case stay as they were.
spec: Plan W6 and Records/Rules ('A correction creates a new revision. It marks dependent tasks and reports stale and links the replacement report; unaffected tasks keep their own snapshot'), Verification 4, and the owner's 'What the agents remember' table and correction test in Dev_Plans/Collaborative_Agentic_Workspace_2026-11-20.md.
plan: dclab_core.memory v3: team scope between person and project, team_scope_id, READS v1 and v2; schemas, baseline v3, CHANGELOG, version 0.165.0, CORE_INTEGRATION section
memory/scope.py: AuthorizedScope.team_ids from the W2 teams store; chain() names only the person's teams; shared_chain() never a team

memory/bases.py: target team:<id> for a team's own base; fact_citation and parse_citation; the problem base's ledger of dependents marked by _mark_dependents_stale in the correction's own write; share_team_fact through upsert_base_fact
memory/summary.py: a team:<id> visibility class built from the team base only, members only, CAS-published

teamspace/store.py: the finder (tasks, reports, recorded decisions citing a fact), transitive staleness, one keyed alert per thread and corrected fact through threads.post; record_decision, stale_marks, decisions
tests on files and PostgreSQL; the existing memory, teamspace, contract and conformance tests; make core-wheel-check

decisions.decision: Team work cites a fact as fact:<entry id>@r<revision>: a task in its allowed inputs, a report in an evidence source, a decision in its constraint revisions.
decisions.why: The team_work contracts already carry these string lists, so no contract changes; an evidence source must be an allowed input, and the citation is both. Entry ids are unique per write, so the revision is a check, not the key.

decisions.decision: Stale marks and recorded decisions live in the problem base's ledger (dependents), not in the team store.
decisions.why: TeamDecision had no store and adding a table needs a migration outside this package; the problem base is where the owner puts decisions and corrections, and a mark written there is in the same write as the correction for every dependent already linked.

decisions.decision: The finder scans the problem's tasks and reports at every correction instead of relying only on links written when the work was saved.
decisions.why: A link written in a second transaction after the team store's would be lost by a crash between them; scanning makes staleness a function of what is stored, and every step (links, marks, the keyed alert, the alerted record) is idempotent, so a later call finishes what a crash left.

decisions.decision: Staleness spreads: a report joining a stale child, a task whose current report is stale, a decision on a stale report.
decisions.why: The owner: 'The shortlist and any approval based on 50 become stale'; an approval often rests on the report, not on the fact directly.

decisions.decision: A team's base is workspace-wide (no project id) and only its members read or edit it; the workspace owner is not a reader.
decisions.why: The owner's table keeps team notes in the team's conversation; a project deletion must not purge a team's notes, and the shared summary must never carry them.

change: dclab_core/memory.py (v3, team scope, team_scope_id), schemas and baseline v3, CHANGELOG and version 0.165.0, CORE_INTEGRATION; dclab_rnd/memory/scope.py (team_ids, team_key, chain/shared_chain/team_chain, with_teams, resolve_scope(teams=)); memory/bases.py (team target, citations, the dependents ledger, link_dependents, mark_alerted, share_team_fact, the post-correction hook); memory/summary.py (read_team_summary); teamspace/store.py (problem_records, record_decision, stale_marks, decisions, mark_fact_dependents_stale); tests/test_team_memory_corrections.py; one assertion in tests/test_problem_memory_active.py. Review fixes: scope.TEAM_STAMP and teams_store, chain() without teams and team_chain(team), the wiring in routers/memory.py, routers/team_threads.py, memory/tools.py and revalidate_job_scope; writing.review refuses team drafts; bases.check_citations, citation_problems, share supersede; store links tasks and reports when made; docs/DATA_CATALOG.md and data_catalog.json regenerated.

findings.defect: A TeamDecision had nowhere to be kept, so a correction could not find a decision built on the old revision.
findings.scenario: Dana approves calling the shortlist on capacity 50; Sales corrects capacity to 30; nothing in the team store holds the decision, so it would stay current
findings.cause: W1 defined TeamDecision but W4 stored only tasks, actions, reports and deliveries
findings.fix: record_decision keeps the decision whole in the problem base's ledger with the fact revisions and reports it rests on; a correction marks it stale and needs_review

findings.defect: Linking a report to the facts it cites only when it is saved would lose the link if the process stopped between the team store's write and the base's.
findings.scenario: a Sales report citing capacity 50 is saved, the process dies before its link is written, capacity is corrected: the report would never be marked stale
findings.fix: every correction runs the finder over the problem's stored tasks and reports, and a late task citing an obsolete revision is stale on arrival; the call can be repeated from any session
findings.test: tests/test_team_memory_corrections.py the late-task part of the 50 to 30 test

findings.defect: The share test expected the team base's revision to be 2 after a fact and a draft.
findings.scenario: Sales writes one fact and proposes one draft, then shares the fact; the test read revision 1 and failed
findings.cause: the test's expectation: a draft never moves a base's revision (only a confirmed change does), as A4 decided
findings.fix: not a defect in the code: the expectation was corrected to revision 1

findings.defect: An existing test pinned the version a v1 item reads as to v2.
findings.scenario: after the bump a v1 item reads as v3 and test_problem_memory_active failed on the label alone
findings.cause: the assertion named the version instead of the contract's current one
findings.fix: the assertion compares with MemoryItem's current schema_version default

findings.defect: A team's memory was lost after storage migrate: its key carried the workspace id the store answers with.
findings.scenario: Sales writes territory exceptions in a file workspace (key local:team_x); the workspace moves to PostgreSQL (w…), the chain asks w…:team_x and finds nothing
findings.cause: team_scope_id(scope.workspace_id, team) while migrate copies items, bases and team ids verbatim
findings.fix: the team key uses one fixed stamp (scope.TEAM_STAMP): the store is already one workspace's and team ids are random

findings.defect: Staleness passed through two steps lost the corrected fact, and a dependent already stale never picked up a second correction.
findings.scenario: child report cites capacity; the parent report joins it; a decision rests on the parent: the decision was stale with no root fact, so the alert never named it for review; a decision stale from the offer correction ignored the later capacity correction
findings.cause: only changes with no via were inherited, and the fix-up skipped refs already stale
findings.fix: inherit every change with a root fact whatever its via; re-link a stale dependent when what it rests on carries a fact it lacks

findings.defect: Recording a decision again (its approval) was not saved, and anyone could replace a decision with another owner.
findings.scenario: Dana's approval is recorded on D-1; reading back shows no approval; Mia records D-1 with herself as owner
findings.cause: the change test counted cites and marks only, and the doc was overwritten without checking its owner
findings.fix: a different doc is a change; a record naming another decision owner is refused

findings.defect: The generated data catalog was stale.
findings.scenario: test_data_catalog failed: DATA_CATALOG.md and data_catalog.json differ from what the code generates
findings.cause: earlier contract changes (and memory_item v3) were not followed by make catalog

findings.defect: Anyone with a reviewer role could accept a team's draft through the memory review.
findings.scenario: Marketing's owner accepts Sales' draft territory exception through POST /api/memory/{id}/review
findings.cause: writing.review checked roles, not team membership
findings.fix: review refuses team drafts: they are confirmed only by a member through bases.confirm_draft

findings.defect: Sharing a team fact silently replaced the problem's fact with the same subject and field.
findings.scenario: Business holds 'No exclusions this quarter'; Sales shares 'Territory North is excluded' and Business's fact is retired unseen
findings.cause: share_team_fact went through upsert_base_fact, which corrects a fact of the same subject and field
findings.fix: refused unless the caller names that entry in supersede

findings.defect: Team work was linked to facts only by the fix-up after a correction; production scopes had no teams; chain() mixed every team; any reader could run the fix-up; a forged revision could mark or hide work.
findings.scenario: the fix-up fails after a correction and the citing task stays current; a person in Sales and Marketing gets both teams' notes in one conversation; a task citing fact@r9 for a fact written at r1
findings.cause: links were made lazily, resolve_scope callers passed no teams store, chain() included teams by default, no write check, citations were not checked
findings.fix: tasks and reports are linked when made or reported (forged or foreign citations refused first); the correction reports a failed fix-up and it can be rerun; teams= wired in the memory routes, tools.chain, _recall, revalidate_job_scope and team_threads; chain() has no team, team_chain(team) reads one; the fix-up needs write rights

outcome: A team now has its own memory that only its members read, a shared summary never carries a team's fact, a share is explicit and sourced, and correcting capacity from 50 to 30 marks exactly the task, report and decision resting on 50, alerts Business once in its own thread, and survives a new session; the kitchen case is unchanged.
lessons: When two stores hold a dependency, make staleness a function of what is stored and keep every side effect keyed, rather than trusting a link written in a second transaction.
A version bump breaks tests that name the version; compare with the contract's current default.
risks: A team's scope id names the workspace, so a file workspace moved to PostgreSQL keeps its team items under the old workspace id until they are rewritten.
A stale mark has no clearing step yet: a task or decision stays stale until R2's recheck flow exists.
